definition: The variety of all life, including different plants and animals, in a particular area or on Earth.
example: Protecting biodiversity is essential for a healthy planet.

definition: A disadvantage or a problem.
example: One drawback of living in a big city is the high cost of living.

definition: To choose someone for a position by voting.
example: Citizens will elect a new president next month.

definition: A public procession, especially one celebrating a special day or event.
example: The city held a big parade to celebrate the national holiday.

definition: To provide financial protection against loss or damage, often by paying money to a company.
example: It's important to insure your car against accidents.

definition: To make sure that something will happen or be the case.
example: Please ensure that all doors are locked before you leave.

definition: Referring to the second of two things or people mentioned.
example: Of the two options, the latter is more expensive.

definition: Referring to the first of two things or people mentioned.
example: The former student is now a successful doctor.

definition: Relating to an early stage in development; very basic or simple.
example: The tools found at the archaeological site were quite primitive.

definition: To protect something from harm or destruction, especially an environmental resource.
example: We need to conserve water during the dry season.

definition: To turn around a central point; or to take turns doing something in a regular sequence.
example: Farmers often rotate their crops to keep the soil healthy.

definition: The act of replacing one thing or person with another.
example: The coach made a substitution in the second half of the game.

definition: A part of a larger whole, especially a serving of food.
example: She only ate a small portion of the cake.

definition: To arrange things into groups or categories based on their type or quality.
example: Please sort the books by author.

definition: An important assignment or purpose, especially one involving travel or a specific goal.
example: The space mission aimed to explore Mars.

definition: A device or piece of equipment designed to perform a specific task, especially in the home.
example: My new kitchen appliance can blend and chop.

definition: To believe that someone is guilty of a crime or involved in a bad action, without having definite proof.
example: The police suspect him of stealing the car.

definition: A result of joining two or more things together.
example: The dish was a delicious combination of sweet and salty flavors.

definition: The science and art of preventing and treating disease; also, a substance used for treating illness.
example: She took some medicine to help with her cold.

definition: A person who has been hurt or killed or who has suffered, either because of the actions of someone else or because of illness or accident.
example: The victim of the accident was taken to the hospital.

definition: A state of confusion or untidiness; also, a disruption of normal physical or mental functions.
example: The room was in complete disorder after the party.

definition: The advantages and disadvantages of something.
example: We discussed the pros and cons of moving to a new city.

definition: A group or system of interconnected people or things, especially for communication or support.
example: She built a strong network of contacts in her industry.

definition: A unit of heredity that is transferred from a parent to offspring and determines a characteristic.
example: Scientists are studying the gene responsible for a specific disease.

definition: To increase in speed or rate.
example: The car accelerated quickly down the highway.

definition: To put something down carefully or flat.
example: He will lay the book on the table.

definition: To prevent someone or something from entering a place, group, or activity.
example: The price excludes tax and delivery.

definition: To focus all one's attention or efforts on a particular object or activity.
example: Please try to concentrate on your studies.

definition: An arrangement with a bank to keep your money; a record of financial transactions.
example: I need to open a new bank account.

definition: Being the only one of its kind; unusually special.
example: Each person has a unique set of fingerprints.

definition: To explain or make something clear by using examples, pictures, or diagrams.
example: The teacher used graphs to illustrate her point.

definition: Not supporting or helping either side in a conflict, disagreement, etc.
example: Switzerland remained neutral during the war.

definition: An important topic or problem for debate or discussion.
example: Climate change is a major issue facing the world today.

definition: In a way that relates to money or finance.
example: The company is financially stable.

definition: Not interesting or exciting; boring.
example: The movie was quite dull, so I fell asleep.

definition: Money received, especially on a regular basis, for work or through investments.
example: Her main income comes from her teaching job.

definition: Arriving or doing something at the agreed or correct time; not late.
example: It's important to be punctual for meetings.

definition: The state of being in a particular place.
example: Your presence at the meeting is required.

definition: Intense and selfish desire for something, especially wealth, power, or food.
example: His greed led him to make bad decisions.

definition: A legally recognized subject or national of a state, either native or naturalized.
example: Every citizen has the right to vote.

definition: Fair behavior or treatment; the quality of being fair and reasonable.
example: The court system aims to ensure justice for everyone.

definition: To put money into a bank account; also, a sum of money placed or kept in a bank account.
example: I need to deposit my paycheck today.

definition: To produce or create something.
example: The new factory will generate many jobs.

definition: Something that is silly or makes no sense.
example: His explanation was pure nonsense.

definition: To hit something hard, causing damage; or a sudden failure of a system or market.
example: The computer system crashed, and we lost our work.

definition: To make something known that was previously secret or hidden.
example: The investigation revealed the truth.

definition: Happening or done immediately.
example: The new software provides instant access to information.

definition: To start or introduce something new, such as a product, project, or rocket.
example: The company plans to launch a new product next month.

definition: The use of remarks that clearly mean the opposite of what they say, used to make fun of someone or something.
example: Her comment was full of sarcasm.

definition: An official rule or law that controls how things are done.
example: The new regulation aims to improve safety.

definition: A painful feeling of humiliation or distress caused by the consciousness of wrong or foolish behavior.
example: She felt deep shame after making such a public mistake.

definition: To make someone annoyed, impatient, or angry.
example: His constant complaining really irritates me.

definition: Physical or mental energy that is needed to do something.
example: You need to make more effort if you want to succeed.

definition: To change from one thing to another.
example: They decided to switch their marketing strategy.

definition: An unpleasant emotion caused by the belief that someone or something is dangerous.
example: He felt a strong fear of heights.

definition: To move someone or something from one place to another.
example: The company will transfer her to a new department.

definition: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger.
example: The country is facing an economic crisis.

definition: Belief in the reliability, truth, ability, or strength of someone or something.
example: It's hard to build trust once it's broken.

definition: A group or set of twelve.
example: I bought a dozen eggs from the store.

definition: A substance used in or produced by a chemical process.
example: The factory produces various chemicals.
